full_judgment:
Mir Hashmat Ali J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Order dated 17-5-2006 passed by the First Court of Settlement, Dhaka in Case No. 362 of 1989 dismissing the case for non-prosecution should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. Thirteen petitioners in the instant Writ Petition challenged the Order dated 17-5-2006 passed by the First Court of Settlement, Dhaka passed in Settlement Case No. 362 of 1989 dismissing the case for non-prosecution at the instance of respondent No.5 without discussing the matter on merit. 

 5. Immediately after liberation of Bangladesh, the aforesaid owner and successors of late Md Faiz Hossain Mia, late Abdul Latif Mia, late Joynal Abedin and late Serajul Islam were at their village home at Keranigonj and the case property was under their lock and key; taking advantage of absence of the owners from the house some miscreants illegally entered into the case property, occupied the same and they made an application to the Sub-Divisional Office (South), Dhaka on 3-12-1973 to release the same and paid Municipal Taxes up to 1973. Subsequently, the case property was enlisted in 'Ka' list of the abandoned property, which was published in Bangladesh Gazette on 23-9-1086. Consequently, the petitioners and other co-sharer filed an application under section 7 of the Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 and it was registered as Settlement Case No. 362 of 1989. Further case of the petitioners are that the aforesaid co-sharer made amicable partition of their joint property along with the case property and the heirs of late Md Faiz Hossain Mia named as Moazzem Hossain, Noor Hossain, Ahmed Hossain, Mosharraf Hossain, Mobarak Hossain and Mozammel Hossain got the case holdingin their share and all the said heirs of late Md Faiz Hossain died except Mobarak Hossain, the petitioner No. 1-3 are the heirs of the said Noor Hossain, the petitioners No. 4-7-are the heirs of late Md Mosharraf Hossain, petitioners No. 8-10 are the heirs of late Md Mozammel Hossain, petitioner No. 11 is the heir of late Ahmed Hossain, and petitioners No. 12-13 are the heirs of late Md Moazzam Hossain. 

 6. The respondent No.4 Md Shahidul Islam is the DN holder of the property in question. The petitioners while in their village home in Keranigonj, in their absence the Court of Settlement dismissed the case for default on 13-11-1991. Against the said Order co-sharers including present petitioner Nos. 4-7,12-13 and respondent No.5 as petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 2129 of 1999 before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court and obtained Rule. After hearing the learned Advocate of the par- ties, the said Rule was made absolute vide judgment and Order dated 29-6-2004 and directed the Court of Settlement to dispose of the case within one month from the date of receipt of the judgment after serving notice to all petitioners. 

 7. The record of the Court of Settlement was sent back to the Court of Settlement, which was received by the Court of Settlement on 13-10-2004. The Court of Settlement was not constituted; the case was fixed for hearing on 9-11-2004 without notifying the parties. The matter was adjourned till 21-3-2006. But the Court of Settlement did not notify the same to all the parties. In the meantime, the respondent No. 5 filed an application before the Court of Settlement on 30-4-2006 without serving copies for all the parties. The said application was heard on 30-4-2006 without notifying all the parties which was subsequently, re-fixed on 17-5-2006 and, after hearing the same, the Court of Settlement, 1st Court of Dhaka vide Order dated 17-5-2006 allowed the application for dismissal the case for non-prosecution. 

 8. The petitioners on 10-4-2007 through one Haji Md Musa came to know for the 1st time that the Court of Settlement dismissed the case for non-prosecution. Then and there the petitioner rushed to the Court of Settlement and after perusal the case record came to know about the dismissal of the case for non-prosecution. 

 9. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application before the Court of Settlement, 1st Court, Dhaka for restoration of the case stating that after the remand Order of the High Court the respondent No.5, Mobarak Hossain filed an application for withdrawal of the case without their consent. The Court of Settlement served no notice to the parties whatsoever or upon any of the co-applicants. 

 10. The petitioners before this Court as applicants filed an application to the Court of settlement for restoration the case. 

 11. The Court of Settlement heard the said application on 15-4-2007 and after hearing the petitioners, the Court of Settlement rejected the application for restoration vide Order dated 15-4-2007 on the ground that the Court of Settlement has no jurisdiction to restore the case. 

 13. Mr MI Faruqui, Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Md Ruhul Quddus and Mr Mohammad Zahid Imam, the learned Advocates for the petitioners submits that under section 10 of the Law of Abandoned Property Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. LIV of 1985) the Court of Settlement has no power to pass any Order for non-prosecution even if prayed for. He further submits that the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 shall not apply to the Court of Settlement and, as such, the Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable, wherein the Court has empowered to withdraw the suit or proceeding. He further submits that our apex Court in their various decisions has decided that after filing of a case before the Court of Settlement, the Court of Settlement has nothing to do but to give decision of the matter. He further submits that Section 10 of the Ordinance No. LIV if 1985 has given procedure for disposal of cases of the Court of Settlement, beyond the said procedure the court of Settlement has no power to dispose of cases even if prayed for. He further submits that in the instant case one of the power holders Mr Mobarak Hossain, who was the applicant before the Court of Settlement filed an application for non-prosecution against the interest of Power of Attorney giver. But the said application was filed beyond the knowledge of the petitioners. The Court of Settlement served no notice to the petitioners as directed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2129 of 1999 and thus the Court of Settlement violated the direction of the High Court Division and committed illegality. He further submits that the Order of non- prosecution or withdrawal of the case, the Court of Settlement has no jurisdiction and thus the Court of Settlement acted beyond its jurisdiction. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Sukurjan Bibi vs Chairman, Court of Settlement, Dhaka reported in 54 DLR 215, the case of Government of the People s Republic of Bangladesh vs Md Shamsul Haque, reported in 56 DLR (AD) 101. 

 14. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman appearing with Md TH Shakil Hossain and Mr Md Khalilur Rahman (Helal) the learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 by submitting affidavit-in-opposition submits that the respondent No.4 purchased the property from one Shibli and entered into the possession of the property. He further submits that though the property in question originally belong to Haji Faiz Hossain, Miah Abdul Latif, Joynal Abedin Miah and Serajul Islam, the predecessors of the petitioners transferred the same to three non-Bengali namely (i) Shamim Ahammed, (ii) Haji Mohammad Omar and (iii) Nafis Ahammed. Lastly in the year 1969 and during liberation war or thereafter said three non-Bengalis left the country for Pakistan deserting their all properties including the case property. Accordingly, the property was devolved upon the Government by operation of PO 16 of 1972. Thereafter; Government sold out the property to five allottees namely Md Nazrul Islam, Haji Emran Hossain, Md Mobarak Hossain, Md Shahidul Islam and Hafiz Akanda by registered deed of trans- fer No. 1920 dated 11-3-1986, 1921 dated 11-3- 1986, 1922 dated 11-3-1986 and 1923 dated 11-3- 1986 respectively. Thereafter the suit property was ultimately devolved upon Md Shafat Imtiaz who transferred 0.0108 acres of land to Haji Shamsul Huque on 18-5-2003 and said Haji Shamsul Huque got approval of the plan from RAJUK for constructing a nine storied building in the said land and also completed the construction of nine storied building. The respondent No.5 for himself and as attorney of others who collusively filed Settlement Case No. 362 of 1989 before the Court of Settlement and ultimately he withdrawn the case by filing application and the Court of Settlement withdrawn the case for non-prosecution. He further submits that since the respondent No. 5 acted for himself and on behalf of other petitioners as power of attorney holder of the petitioners all act done by the respondent No. 5 in respect of the case-property is binding upon all others petitioners. He further submits that who has filed the case, he has power to withdraw the case and the Court of Settlement passed the Order in accordance with law and thereby committed no illegality. He further submits that the petitioners claim that they have inherited the case property but fact remains that the predecessor of the petitioners already transferred their share in favour of three non-Bengali namely Haji Mohammad Omar, Shamim Ahmed and  Nafiz Ahmed and, as such, the petitioners have no interest in the case property. He further submits that the casebefore the Court of settlement is a fruitless litigation and Court should not allow continuing to a fruitless litigation. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Sanatannessa Bewa vs Haipatullah Sarkar reported in 41 DLR (AD) 105. 

 17. We have also perused the impugned Order dated 17-5-2006 Annexures-'B' series. We find that the settlement case was dismissed forenoon-prosecution against which the petitioner obtained this Rule. To consider the matter let us see the sequence of the case. It appears that the petitioners filed Settlement Case No. 362 of 1989 before the Court of Settlement under section 7 of the Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. 54 of 1985). The said case was dismissed for default due to the absence of the petitioners. Being aggrieved the petitioners filed Writ Petition No. 2129 of 1999 before this Court and the said, Rule was made absolute and the said Order of dismissal for default dated 13-11-1991 was declared illegal and the Court of Settlement directed to dispose of the case within one month from the date of receipt of the judgment after notifying the parties. The said direction was received by the Court of Settlement on 13-10-2004. But the petitioners were not notified by the Court of Settlement and several dates were adjourned due to non-availability of appointment of member and appointment of lawyer for conducting the case of the Government. 

 19. In paragraph No. 16 of the Writ Petition, the petitioners claimed that there is no consent of the petitioners for filing an application for non-prosecution of the settlement case. 

 20. It further appears that no notice was served upon the petitioners for the same. But the Court of Settlement dismissed the case for non-prosecution. 

 21. Let us see, whether Court of Settlement is authorised to dismiss a case for non-prosecution. Section 10 of Law of Abandoned Property Ordinance (Ordinance No. 54 of 1985) has been enacted for the purpose of Power and Procedure of Court of Settlement for disposal of a case. 

 Power and procedure of Court of Settlement- 

 10. Power and procedure of Court of Settlement: 

 (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Ordinance, the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1903 (Act V of 1908), shall not apply to a Court of Settlement. 

 (2) For the purpose of hearing an application, a Court of Settlement shall have all the powers of a Civil Court, while trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908), in respect of the following matters, namely:- 

 (3) Any proceeding before a Court of Settlement shall be deemed to be a judicial proceeding within the meaning of section 193 of the Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860). 

 (4) A Court of Settlement shall hold its sit- tings at such place or places as the Government may fix. 

 (5) A Court of Settlement shall, after such enquiry as it may deem necessary and after giving reasonable opportunity to the parties concerned of being heard and also adducing evidence, both oral and documentary, if any, make such decision on the prayer of the applicant as it deems fit. 

 (6) The decision on [of] the Court of Settlement shall be final and shall be binding on all parties concerned and shall not be called in question in any other Court. 

 (7) No appeal shall lie from any Order of decision of the Court of Settlement to any other Court of authority. 

 23. From the above, we find that the Court of Settlement has no power to use the provisions of Civil Procedure Code. Since the Civil Procedure Code is not applicable in the cases pending before Court of Settlement. In this regard Order XXIII of the Civil Procedure Code wherein the provisions of withdrawal of cases has been enacted is not applicable for the Court of Settlement. It further appears from sub section 5 of section 10 of the said Ordinance, which has made mandatory upon the Court of Settlement to make decision as it deems fit and, as such, it is clear that the Court of Settlement is to dispose of the case on the basis of the materials before it notwithstanding the fact that the petitioner is absent or took no steps. This view has already been supported in various decisions of this Court. In the case of Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and another reported in 56 DLR (AD) 101, which has been held that; "It appears from the .impugned Order that the Court of Settlement dismissed the case for default and that although the law requires decision is to be given as to whether the enlistment of the abandoned building have been done legally or not and accordingly, the High Court Division rightly sent the case back on remand for deciding the issue in the light of the observation made therein". 

 24. Whether the property in question is abandoned or not is to be decided by the Court of Settlement not by any other Court. Similar view was taken in the case of Sukurjan Bibi vs Chairman, Court of Settlement, Dhaka reported in 54 DLR 215. Wherein it has been held that: 

 "There is no scope for the Court of Settlement to pass an ex-parte Order of dismissal for default as the Court of Settlement is required to give a decision on the issues raised by the parties ." 

 25. Similar view was also taken in the case of Shamima Begum vs Chairman, Court of Settlement reported in 52 DLR 456, the case of Chand Miah Talukder vs Chairman, Court of Settlement, Bangladesh Abandoned Building reported in 45 DLR 304, the case of Bangladesh vs Feroz Ahmed reported in I BLC (AD) 149. 

 27. Whether the petitioners have got no interest and title over the case property or they are fighting for a fruitless litigation is the matter of evidence which is to be decided by the Court of Settlement itself after recording of evidences adduce by the respective parties at the time of trial of the case, not by this Court and, as such, we do not find any sub- stance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 and thus the decisions cited by him are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. 

 28. In the earlier judgment passed in Writ Petition No. 2129 of 1999, the Court of Settlement was directed to dispose of the case within one month from the date of receipt of the judgment after notifying the parties concerned. But the Court of Settlement without notifying all the concerned parties passed an Order of dismissal for non-prosecution and that all the parties were not aware of any application for non-prosecution. Since the Court of Settlement is not empowered to apply Order XXIII of the Code of Civil Procedure and since in several decisions it has been settled that the Court of Settlement is to give decision to its cases, there is no provision for dismissal for non-prosecution or dismissal for default and, as such, the impugned Order of dismissal for non-prosecution is liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 29. The learned Advocate for the petitioners submitted that it is not possible for the Court of Settlement to dispose of the case within one month after notifying all the parties concern and prayed for a direction to dispose of the case after notifying all the parties preferably within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and Order of this Court. 

 30. Considering the submissions, we feel that the justice will be met if we direct the Court of Settlement to dispose of the case after notifying all the parties concern preferably within 3(three) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and Order. 

 31. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without any Order as to the cost. The Court of Settlement is directed to give decision of the case after notifying all the parties concerned preferably within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of this Judgment and Order.
